## Intended repository tree

```text
scgsim/
├── README.md                 # SCGSim Development-owned package entry
├── _quarto.yml               # SCGSim Development-owned site configuration
├── _extensions/              # SCGSim Development-owned vendored Quarto extensions
├── docs/                     # SCGSim Development-owned authored Quarto sources/assets
├── src/scgsim/               # SCGSim Development-owned product source
├── schemas/                  # SCGSim Development-owned product schemas
├── scripts/                  # SCGSim Development-owned producers/tooling
└── tests/                    # SCGSim Development-owned stabilization tests
```

Generated site output is never source authority.

## Responsibility map

| Owner | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| SCGSim Development | Package/build/runtime/report source, schemas, tests, scripts, CI/release, README, Quarto site configuration and extensions, authored documentation and assets, information architecture and prose, generated-reference placement/presentation |
| OrPen SC PDK | Public PDK facts, public Component source, and public component-simulation notebooks |
| Chip Design EPR | Surface-EPR requirements and private consumer validation only |
| `scq-ansys-aedt` | Version-locked AEDT/PyAEDT procedure only; no repository path ownership |
| Integration & Sync | Repository settings, merges, future pins, synchronization, and cleanup |

Generated API reference may be produced from product-owned source, while its
placement and presentation remain package-owned. No owner listed here may
infer Human acceptance, publication authority, or merge authority from a green
build.

## Public documentation site

The canonical site is `https://orpenstrike.github.io/scgsim/`; it is the
version landing page. The current development home is
`https://orpenstrike.github.io/scgsim/develop/`. A `/main/` home is reserved
until a `main` branch exists and has been published. Do not advertise a dead
`/main/` link or create version archives as part of routine documentation
maintenance.

The **Documentation Pages** GitHub Actions workflow owns publication. Pushes
to `develop` or `main`, and a manual `workflow_dispatch`, start one combined
build. At build start, `scripts/build_docs_site.py` resolves and records the
current remote commit for each available branch. It renders clean tracked
snapshots separately with Quarto 1.10.18 and code execution disabled, then
publishes one artifact containing the version landing page and available
branch homes. Each branch page and `build.json` record its package version and
source commit. Pull requests do not publish. Generated site output is not
committed to either branch.

If a branch render fails, the publish step must not run; the last successfully
published site remains in place. Read the failing Actions run and its build
logs, fix the tracked source or configuration, and push the correction to the
same branch. For a one-off rebuild without a new commit, open **Actions →
Documentation Pages → Run workflow** and select `develop` (or `main` once it
exists). The workflow rebuilds the combined artifact from then-current remote
heads; uncommitted local changes are not included. If deployment itself fails,
inspect the deploy job and the `github-pages` environment, correct the setup,
then run the workflow again. Repository Pages settings and the environment are
owned by Integration & Sync.

For a local diagnostic build, use Python 3.12, network access to GitHub, and
Quarto 1.10.18. The helper reads remote commits rather than the local working
tree, and `--output` must name a new directory:

```bash
preview_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
rmdir "$preview_dir"
python scripts/build_docs_site.py --output "$preview_dir"
```

Do not upload local output by hand or bypass the workflow with a Pages branch
or personal access token.
